title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics across python/typescript/go + parity & v1.132.1 bumps
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: This PR unifies the auth and retry ergonomics across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, stabilizes the streaming APIs to match behavior across languages, fixes several parity gaps identified by the SDK compatibility matrix, and bumps SDK package versions to v1.132.1.

Motivation: divergent auth & retry behaviors caused inconsistent developer experience and intermittent production call differences (token refresh timing, backoff jitter). We standardize behavior to the platform spec (token refresh proactive window, exponential + full-jitter backoff, deterministic stream close semantics).

Checklist:
- [x] Define canonical auth flow and token-refresh window (30s)
- [x] Implement unified retry policy across SDKs (max_retries=5, base=100ms, max_backoff=2s, full jitter)
- [x] Stabilize streaming disconnect/EOF handling and reconnection guidance
- [x] Merge small parity fixes (response shape, error wrapping)
- [x] Bump versions (python: 1.132.1, ts: 1.132.1, go: 1.132.1)
- [x] Update CHANGELOGs and release notes

Key changes and rationale:
- Auth: introduce a shared token refresh helper pattern (proactive refresh, single in-flight refresh per process) to prevent thundering refreshes. Python and TS expose the refresh hook for advanced use; Go uses the same semantics via a refreshed token provider interface. Rationale: reduces 401 spikes observed under high-concurrency.
- Retries: adopt standardized retry policy module in each SDK with identical parameters and observability hooks (retry_count metric, last_error tag). This fixes discrepancies where TS retried on 5xx but Python retried on 429/5xx; now all three follow the same set and backoff strategy.
- Streaming: normalize close semantics so client-streamed EOF is delivered to the server before stream termination; add clear reconnection guidance and idempotency notes to docs. Also fix a bug where TypeScript client emitted duplicate 'end' events under network flaps.
- Parity fixes: response metadata keys normalized (camelCase -> snake_case mapping kept internal), error types unified (SDKError base type with code/ops fields), consistent content-type handling for structured outputs.
- Version bumps: package metadata updates, changelogs, and smoke tests.

Commits (high-level):
- unify(auth): introduce shared refresh helper and retry config
- sdk/python: refactor auth provider, add retry module, streaming tests
- sdk/typescript: align retry predicates, fix streaming end event dedupe, update types
- sdk/go: implement token provider interface, unify error wrapping
- docs: update changelogs and quickstarts
- tests: add cross-language parity e2e harness

Review conversation (high level):
- Maya Chen: "Can we add a small integration test exercising token refresh under high concurrency?" \u2014 Added a focused e2e stress test and metric assertions.
- Diego Rivera: "TS type exports look good but check `AbortSignal` propagation in streaming." \u2014 Fixed propagation and added unit.
- Sven Larsson: "Please ensure bumping versions updates marketplace docs and runtimes." \u2014 Confirmed in changelog and release checklist.

CI notes: initial run showed a flaky e2e (integration-tests) failing on TS streaming duplicate 'end' event; flaky was fixed by dedupe patch and subsequent rerun passed. All unit, lint, and typechecks passed.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals and all CI green; release cut followed on the same day.

Release notes: "sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go. Standardized retry/backoff semantics, proactive token refresh, streaming close semantics, parity fixes, and package bumps to v1.132.1."

Additional context: This unification should reduce cross-language diffs observed in downstream apps and reduce operational surprises (friction from differing retry windows and token refresh).
